source_review.evidence: Accepted only for the candidate proof-edge binding and current lesson. Directly checked Chewi arXiv:2605.07006v1 §1.2, Definition 1.5, Proposition 1.6 and displayed proof at HTML lines 198–244. The scoped formula and proof route agree. The canonical verdict compares with the entire source proposition and deliberately records incomplete source coverage. The current module defines path(t)=x+t(y−x), rewrites hsc.2 along it, obtains the segment derivative from hgrad x hx via HasFDerivAt/HasLineDerivAt, and invokes the named scalar-limit parent. The lesson accurately explains positive division and the one-sided derivative limit supplied by that parent. The source-blind reconstruction matches all visible premises and the conclusion. I did not independently rerun compilation or inspect the scalar-limit parent; compiled=true is packet evidence, not a new build certification. Supplementary pinned-source inspection: Independently inspected the supplied unmodified raw upstream file at the packet-pinned commit. Its header identifies copyright 2023 Chenyi Li, authors Chenyi Li and Ziyu Wang, and Apache 2.0. The file section retains CompleteSpace E and arbitrary real m; the earlier mp variable is unused in the target declarations. Strong_Convex_second_lower has exactly the same domain-local StrongConvexOn and ambient HasGradientAt assumptions, endpoint quantifiers, and m/2 lower-model conclusion. Upstream proves these through subtraction of a norm-square and convex-gradient APIs; ASTIS explicitly uses its own geodesic-limit parent and two endpoint bounds. Statement provenance and attribution are supported. No upstream build or complete dependency audit is asserted.
